thread.title: Johnson & Johnson to wield Apple Watch for health-tech study

author: Anthony Noto
title: Johnson & Johnson to wield Apple Watch for health-tech study
text: – Reporter, New York Business Journal Jan 18, 2019, 10:11am EST Johnson & Johnson (J&J) is teaming up with Apple Inc. on a new health-tech initiative. The two companies are hoping to wield the Apple Watch to help pinpoint early irregular heart conditions before something life-threatening happens. J&J (NYSE: JNJ), based in New Brunswick, New Jersey, announced Thursday that a research study was in the works through its subsidiary Janssen Pharmaceuticals Inc. The goal is to use its J&J-developed heart health monitoring app on the latest Apple Watch series to will help people living with atrial fibrillation. Paul Stoffels , J&J's chief scientific officer, praised the partnership: We’re excited about the potential of common, wearable technology to aid in the earlier detection and prevention of a frequent cause of stroke. Too many people living with AFib are unaware of their risk, and earlier detection, diagnosis and treatment of AFib could significantly improve outcomes. Based on the insights generated through this research program, we may be able to develop new ways to detect other health conditions earlier in the future that also exhibit measurable physiological symptoms. J&J has maintained that neither the company nor Apple will have access to identifiable patient data ( h/t The Wall Street Journal ). The company also says it will not make any information available to third-party providers, such as healthcare systems or insurers. J&J purchased Janssen in the 1960s. Since then, it has expanded the subsidiary with various M&A deals, including the 2017 purchase of Actelion Ltd for a total purchase price of $30 billion in cash. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), meanwhile, continues to incorporate healthcare and wellness as a core part of its app, services, and wearables strategies. The Cupertino, California-based company has been ramping up research in the medical device space . In the past, Apple has collaborated with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for a pilot program to help the agency figure out how to regulate lower-risk digital health products. It also inked a partnership with health insurer Aetna to get discounted Apple Watches into the hands of its members. – Reporter, New York Business Journal Jan 18, 2019, 10:11am EST Related Content
